perspective:
From Harold Padilla’s subjective viewpoint, he has access to:

- He is a project manager whose project progress seems affected by his team appearing unmotivated. He feels frustrated, anxious, and “at his wit’s end.”
- He knows Arthur Begum as a trusted friend/advisor, a police officer whom he often relies on for advice and support in stressful situations.
- In their coffee-shop meeting, Harold tells Arthur his team seems unmotivated and asks for advice. He hears Arthur suggest understanding each team member individually, having one-on-one conversations, and making people feel valued and understood personally.
- Harold admits to Arthur that he had focused on project goals and deadlines rather than personal motivations. He decides to try Arthur’s advice and feels more hopeful and relieved.
- In a team meeting, Harold proposes one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each member. He hears Team Member 1 say it could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they are open to it. Harold says he will schedule time with each person and wants the project to succeed together.
- Later, Harold observes that the team still is not responding well to the new strategies. He feels disappointed and worried about the project’s future.
- He tells Arthur he tried the suggestions but the team still is not responding well. He hears Arthur say there may be deeper issues, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold may need to dig deeper.
- Harold says he had not thought of that, asks what issues Arthur means, and after hearing examples decides to set up another round of meetings to find the root causes.
- Harold feels determined and focused, believes there may be underlying team issues he has not addressed, and decides to investigate team dynamics more deeply through one-on-one meetings.
- In those one-on-one meetings, Harold says he has noticed performance issues and wants to understand concerns. He hears Team Member 1 say there is tension between a few team members affecting work. Harold says he will look into resolving conflicts. He hears Team Member 2 say they feel overwhelmed by workload and stressed, making motivation hard. Harold says he understands and will see if tasks can be redistributed, saying their well-being matters.
- Harold feels optimistic and empowered, believes addressing individual concerns will improve performance, and intends to create a more supportive, open team environment with regular feedback sessions and team-building activities.
- In the final team meeting, Harold tells the team he has heard their concerns and will implement regular feedback sessions and team-building. He hears Team Member 1 say it sounds great and will help, and Team Member 2 agree that their concerns are being addressed. Harold says he is glad and urges the team to work together, saying their input and well-being are crucial to success.
